title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS FEATURES. Original 9 were cut to 6, framed as three jobs: Win the deal (RFP), Run the work (ActionSwarm, IT access, search), Control the spend (expenses, Zombie SaaS). F1 RFP and Security Questionnaire Engine (the wedge, real build): upload Excel/CSV, knowledge base of SOC2 docs/policies, answer per question with citation, confidence gate (auto-fill above threshold, red flag below with closest source), human review UI, learning loop (corrected answers saved and reused on next questionnaire), export .xlsx plus accuracy report. F2 ActionSwarm (real): meeting transcript to schema-forced JSON of action items, assignees, due dates; tasks on own dashboard board (real Jira optional); Slack summary post; email draft; live activity feed; injection guard that treats planted instructions as data. F3 OmniContext + Catch-Me-Up (Cmd+K, real over ~10 seeded docs): hybrid search with cited answers, permission-aware retrieval (intern vs founder salary-sheet demo; needs confirmation that Meko datapack sharing supports this), Catch-Me-Up is a time-window mode ("last 4 days") giving an executive briefing. F4 ZeroTouch Expenses (thin): 3-5 prepared receipts via Gemini vision, extract merchant/items/GST/total, policy check, one violation, card-feed matching. F5 Zero-Friction IT Provisioning (real logic): natural-language request ("I need Figma"), risk classification, role check, low-risk auto-grant, high-risk (AWS prod) manager Approve/Reject (dashboard button, Slack button if time), audit log and undo. F6 Zombie SaaS Eradicator (mocked on purpose): seeded billing and SSO login tables, one SQL join for tools paid for with zero logins in 30+ days, waste dashboard in rupees. CUT (roadmap slide only): Dynamic Pitch-Deck Compiler, Procurement and Contract Routing. Priority: RFP engine plus trust layer must never be cut; cut order if behind: Zombie SaaS, Expenses, Slack buttons, Catch-Me-Up. On slides use feature names, not numbers.

title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS CLAIMS TO AVOID AND HONESTY RULES. Do NOT claim: SOC 2 or DPDP compliance (say "designed for DPDP alignment; SOC 2 is the first milestone once enterprise pilots begin"); zero data retention today (ZDR is an agreement arranged with the provider for production; the demo runs on Gemini's free tier whose data terms may allow training on prompts, so drop ZDR from the pitch); "never stored" (our own tables store data; only say the model provider's retention is a separate matter); any productivity percentages or stats we did not measure (cut "40% of the workweek", "15 hours per employee per week", "pays for itself on Day 1", "95%", "under 60 seconds" unless measured); unverified competitor limits (check Copilot, Glean, ServiceNow, Coupa, Loopio, Zluri pages first); a made-up market size. Say plainly what is built live versus simulated (Zombie SaaS and SSO logs seeded; Jira-style tickets on our own board; Slack real if time) before judges ask. Prompt injection is not solved industry-wide; do not call it bulletproof. Prefer quoting our own measured numbers (e.g. "50 questions in X seconds, Y auto-answered, Z flagged; precision of auto-filled answers W%"). Differentiation line: each incumbent covers a slice inside its own suite; Plexus is the neutral, vendor-agnostic layer with one shared memory and one approval and audit layer across departments. Business model: per-seat for small and mid teams, department-level pilots then enterprise contracts for large companies, usage-based for heavy automation; land with the RFP wedge.

title: Knowledge Doc
content:
Demo order (about 3 minutes, tuned to Meko's strengths)

Drop in the Meridian RFP sheet; cells fill, a few turn red.

Fix one red cell as a human; run a second questionnaire and show that cell now fills itself. Say: what one agent learns, every agent knows.

Upload the kickoff transcript; tasks, a Slack post and an email draft stream into the feed. Include the planted injection line and show it blocked.

4. A new hire asks for Figma (instant) and AWS production (manager approval).

5. Open the audit screen and click one action to show its trace: prompt, sources, confidence, undo.

6. Cmd+K: Catch me up on Meridian. Then, if built, the receipt and Zombie SaaS tabs in 15 seconds.

Claims to avoid: any SOC 2 or DPDP compliance claim, zero data retention, "never stored", and productivity percentages you did not measure.
